summary: Use a Balance to show one money amount, such as what someone owes or holds, in large type under a short title.

useWhen.text: Show one money amount, such as what someone owes or holds, in large type under a short title.

from.quote: Use a Balance to show one money amount, such as what someone owes or holds, in large type under a short title.

avoidWhen.text: An amount people press, or one that needs a selected, disabled or loading look: a Balance isn't pressable and has none of those looks.

from.quote: A Balance isn’t pressable and has no selected, disabled, or loading look.

anatomy.holds: title: names the amount in 14 px medium text.

from.quote: Names the amount in 14 px medium text.

anatomy.holds: The symbol for your currency code (currency), such as ₹ for INR. Your own Money Value in children replaces the default one.

from.quote: The symbol for your currency code, such as ₹ for INR.

anatomy.holds: amount, exactly as you write it, in 36 px heavy type at the default size.

from.quote: Your amount exactly as you write it, in 36 px heavy type.

placementAdvice.text: Place a Balance in a screen or card that has padding and a surface: it has neither of its own.

from.quote: It has no padding or surface, so place it in a screen or card that has them.

placementAdvice.text: The host sets the width: a Balance is as wide as its host and as tall as its text, 68 px at the default size.

from.quote: A Balance is as wide as its host and as tall as its text: 68 px at the default size.

placementAdvice.text: In a column host, such as a screen or a VStack, a Balance takes the host's width and a long title wraps. In a row host it is as wide as its text, so a long title runs past the host on one line.

from.quote: in a column host (a screen, a VStack, Storybook's padded View) the Balance takes the host's width and a long title wraps

placementAdvice.text: In the guide’s trip screen, Settle up is the screen’s own Button, not part of the Balance.

from.quote: Settle up is the screen’s own Button.

rules.text: One amount, named, at a glance.

rules.text: Write the title as a short name for the amount, such as “Available balance” or “Total owed to people”.

from.quote: Write the title as a short name for the amount, such as “Available balance” or “Total owed to people”.

rules.text: Pass the amount already formatted, with separators and decimals: the Balance shows it exactly as you write it.

from.quote: Pass the amount already formatted, with separators and decimals: the Balance shows it exactly as you write it.

rules.text: Name the amount: “Available balance” says what the number is.

from.quote: “Available balance” says what the number is.

rules.text: Keep the title short: two or three words name the amount.

from.quote: Two or three words name the amount.

rules.text: Do not leave the default title: a savings balance would still say “Total owed to people”.

from.quote: A savings balance still says “Total owed to people”.

rules.text: Do not write a sentence as the title: a long title wraps and buries the amount.

from.quote: A long title wraps and buries the amount.

rules.text: Do not pass a raw number such as 124500.5: the Balance doesn't format, so it shows as written.

examples.purpose: What you owe after a trip, the guide's In context: the screen adds up the amount and passes it as formatted text, the Balance shows it under the screen's Title, and Settle up is the screen's own Button.
examples.jsx:
<VStack>
  <Title title="Goa trip" subtitle="4 friends · 12 expenses" />
  <VStack>
    <Balance title="Total owed to people" amount="2,450.00" currency="INR" />
    <Button label="Settle up" onPress={() => {}} />
  </VStack>
</VStack>

from.quote: Settle up is the screen’s own Button.

props.name: title
props.description: An empty title still leaves an 18 px line and the 6 px gap above the amount. Declared: Title text displayed above the balance amount. Default "Total owed to people", from the component source.

props.name: amount
props.description: Shown exactly as passed: no grouping or decimals are added. A leading minus is drawn as its own sign before the symbol. Declared: Amount to display in the balance. Default "50,000.67", from the component source.

props.name: currency
props.description: ISO codes map to their symbols (INR ₹, USD $, EUR € and others); unknown codes print as typed. Declared: Currency symbol or code. Default "₹", from the component source.

props.name: style
props.description: Optional style overrides for the container.

props.name: children
props.description: Optional children content to render instead of the default MoneyValue. Use this slot for custom money value implementations.

props.name: testID
props.description: Native / testing id for the root.

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: Accessible name for the title-and-amount block.

props.name: ...Omit<React.ComponentProps<typeof View>, 'children' | 'style'>
props.description: Inherited React Native props the component also accepts. They are not part of the design contract and no guide documents them.

modes.name: Color Mode
modes.description: A token collection Balance reads (the package's FIGMA_COMPONENT_MODES). When modes leave it unset, the resolver uses the collection's default mode.

modes.name: Context3
modes.description: Sets the amount's size; the title stays 14 px. Balance's Money Value defaults to Balance & Cards, not the collection's Default: a 36 px symbol and amount at weight 900 on a 44 px line. Default gives a 14 px amount, Transaction Bubble a 26 px amount with a 28 px symbol, Amount Input a 56 px amount with a 32 px symbol. Balance's modes can change the default Money Value's Context3, but a slotted Money Value always gets Balance & Cards. Declared: A token collection Balance reads (the package's FIGMA_COMPONENT_MODES). When modes leave it unset, the resolver uses the collection's default mode.

modes.name: Page type
modes.description: JioPlus turns the amount white, and the title with it. Declared: A token collection Balance reads (the package's FIGMA_COMPONENT_MODES). When modes leave it unset, the resolver uses the collection's default mode.

slots.name: children
slots.description: Children replace the default Money Value; amount and currency are then ignored. Declared: Optional children content to render instead of the default MoneyValue. Use this slot for custom money value implementations.

gaps.text: Figma's Balance is one component with a Title property and a nested Money Value, whose amount and currency are overrides. In code amount and currency are props, and children takes your own Money Value.
The package draws the amount on a 44 px line where Figma's is 36 px, so a Balance is 68 px tall instead of Figma's 60.
